Package Setup & Maintenace

library(rpkgkit)

dir <- tempdir()
usethis::create_package(path = dir, open = FALSE)

Create package infrastructure

A startup message

use_zzz() creates a package documentation file with .onLoad, .onAttach, and %||%. It is similar to usethis::use_package_doc() while also providing a useful starting template.

use_zzz(path = dir, open = FALSE)
#> ✔ Setting active project to "/tmp/RtmplqzxOK".
#> ✔ Created /tmp/RtmplqzxOK/R/RtmplqzxOK-package.R from template.
#> ✔ Adding cli to Imports field in DESCRIPTION.
#> 
#> ☐ Refer to functions with `cli::fun()`.

Check missing function in _pkgdown reference

check_pkgdown_reference() identifies exported functions that are absent from the reference section of _pkgdown.yml.

check_pkgdown_reference(pkg = dir)

Configure the clangd language server

use_clangd() writes a .clangd configuration file that lets the clangd language server find the system R headers and the include/ directory of the packages you pass in include (Rcpp, RcppEigen and RcppArmadillo by default). Packages that are not installed are skipped with a warning.

use_clangd(path = dir, overwrite = TRUE)
#> Warning: Package RcppEigen is not installed; skipping its
#> include path.
#> Warning: Package RcppArmadillo is not installed; skipping its
#> include path.
#> ✔ Created /tmp/RtmplqzxOK/.clangd.

When path is a package root, the file also disables background indexing for the R/ directory (which holds no C++ code) and adds .clangd to .Rbuildignore.

use_clangd(path = dir, include = c("Rcpp", "BH"), overwrite = TRUE)
#> ! Overwriting /tmp/RtmplqzxOK/.clangd.
#> Warning: Package BH is not installed; skipping its include path.
#> ✔ Created /tmp/RtmplqzxOK/.clangd.

Configure the jarl linter

use_jarl() writes a jarl.toml file for jarl, the linter written in Rust. The file pins down the linting behaviour of every jarl invocation, so the command line, your editor and CI all agree. It enables the opt-in TESTTHAT group of rules, skips vendored files, and lints the code inside @examples and @examplesIf tags.

use_jarl(path = dir, overwrite = TRUE)
#> ✔ Created /tmp/RtmplqzxOK/jarl.toml.
#> • Read jarl's editor support
#>   (<https://jarl.etiennebacher.com/reference/config-file>) to learn how to
#>   invoke jarl in your preferred editor.
#> 
#> • Read jarl's continuous integration
#>   (<https://jarl.etiennebacher.com/howto/ci>) to learn about GHA workflows that
#>   continuously run linting checks.

jarl reads a single configuration file: the closest jarl.toml in the current directory or any of its parents, and finally the one in your user configuration directory. When path is a package root, jarl.toml is also added to .Rbuildignore so it stays out of the built tarball.

readLines(file.path(dir, "jarl.toml")) |> cli::cli_code()
#> # jarl configuration file
#> # Reference: https://jarl.etiennebacher.com/reference/config-file
#> [lint]
#> # Rules enabled on top of jarl's default rule set. The `TESTTHAT` group is
#> # opt-in, so it has to be requested explicitly.
#> extend-select = ["TESTTHAT"]
#> # Files or directories that jarl should not lint.
#> exclude = ["R/vendor-*.R"]
#> # Also lint the R code inside `@examples` and `@examplesIf` tags
#> # (the default).
#> check-roxygen = true
#> # Rules that `jarl check --fix` is allowed to fix (all rules by default).
#> # fixable = ["PERF"]
#> # Rules that `jarl check --fix` must leave untouched.
#> # unfixable = ["undesirable_function"]

Read the configuration reference for options such as select, ignore and per-file-ignores, and the continuous integration guide to run jarl check on every push with the etiennebacher/setup-jarl action.

Vendor permissively licensed code

use_vendor() records attribution and licensing information when incorporating selected source files from a permissively licensed GitHub R package. It creates an inst/vendor/ directory, a R/vendor-*.R file, and updates relevant DESCRIPTION fields.

try(use_vendor(
  pkg = "WangLabCSU/rpkgkit",
  "43_use_vendor.R",
  branch = "main",
  path = dir
))
#> ℹ Fetching repository information for WangLabCSU/rpkgkit...
#> ✔ Vendor package uses MIT license.
#> ✔ Created directory /tmp/RtmplqzxOK/inst/vendor/rpkgkit.
#> ✔ Copied LICENSE.
#> ✔ Copied LICENSE.md.
#> ✔ Created inst/vendor/rpkgkit/README.md.
#> ✔ Created /tmp/RtmplqzxOK/R/vendor-rpkgkit.R.
#> ✔ Added rpkgkit authors to Authors@R.
#> ✔ Updated DESCRIPTION.
#> ☐ Consider pasting the following statement into README.md
#> 
#> 
#> ## Acknowledgements
#> 
#> We would like to thank the following people and projects:
#> 
#> - The authors of the [rpkgkit](https://github.com/WangLabCSU/rpkgkit) package &mdash; **Yuxi Yang** &mdash; whose code is included (under MIT license) in files named `vendor-rpkgkit.*`.

Only packages with a supported permissive license can be vendored. Review the acknowledgement text printed by the function and add it to your README when appropriate.

usethis extensions

Use the following helpers from the package root:

Use R 4.1.0 version

R 4.1.0 introduced the pipe (|>) and anonymous function \(). If these syntaxes need to be used in a package, the R package must require at least R version 4.1.0.

use_r_v4.1.0(path = dir)
#> ✔ Adding R to Depends field in DESCRIPTION.

Add URL in DESCRIPTION 

use_url(dir)

Add bug reports URL in DESCRIPTION 

use_bugreports(dir)

Open CFF

CITATION.cff files are plain text files with human- and machine-readable citation information for software and datasets.

Code developers can include such files in their source code repositories to let others know how to correctly cite their software.

open_cffinit()

This cannot replace usethis::use_citation(), it just complements project.

Global ignore-file templates

Use add_global_rbuildignore() and add_global_gitgnore() to add the corresponding global ignore-file templates to a package.

add_global_rbuildignore(path = dir)
#> ✔ Added 38 pattern(s) to .Rbuildignore.
add_global_gitgnore(pkg = dir)

GitHub Actions workflows

Each use_workflow_*() function copies a workflow template bundled in inst/actions/ into the .github/ directory of the target package. All of them create the directories they need, abort instead of overwriting unless overwrite = TRUE, and return the written path invisibly.

Bump the version from commit messages

use_workflow_version_update() installs version_update.yml together with the version-bumper composite action. The version is bumped from the commit message (major/breaking, feat/minor, patch/fix), or explicitly through workflow_dispatch. A bump is skipped when the new version would exceed the highest version documented in NEWS.md, and the version field of src/rust/Cargo.toml is kept in sync when the package ships Rust code.

use_workflow_version_update(path = dir)
#> ✔ Created workflow: /tmp/RtmplqzxOK/.github/workflows/version_update.yml
#> → It triggers on push to "main/master" and via workflow_dispatch. Version bump
#>   is inferred from commit messages or manual input.
#> ☐ It is recommended to add a devel version badge to your README.md via
#> `badger::badge_devel(color = "blue")`

Run R CMD check on packages with Rust code

use_workflow_rust_compatible_check() installs a R-CMD-check.yaml that can download, compile and link Rust crates, which is what packages built on extendr/rextendr need. It replaces usethis::use_github_action("check-standard") for such packages.

use_workflow_rust_compatible_check(path = dir)
#> ✔ Created workflow: /tmp/RtmplqzxOK/.github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml
#> → It triggers on push to "main" and on pull requests targeting "main".
#> → Rust crates are compiled with a pinned toolchain and the
#>   "x86_64-pc-windows-gnu" target on Windows, so they link against Rtools.

The difference lies in the toolchain. The usethis workflow only sets up R and leaves the runner default in place; on Windows that default is an MSVC toolchain, while R and Rtools are GNU based, so the static library produced by cargo cannot be linked and the resulting build noise makes R CMD check report a WARNING. The template used here follows the official extendr CI:

  • dtolnay/rust-toolchain installs the requested toolchain and, on Windows, additionally the x86_64-pc-windows-gnu target that Rtools can link.
  • The matrix covers Windows, macOS, Ubuntu release and Ubuntu devel with fail-fast: false, so one broken platform does not hide the others.
  • R_REMOTES_NO_ERRORS_FROM_WARNINGS keeps download noise from remotes and pak from surfacing as a check failure.

Sync main to a test branch

use_workflow_test_branch() adds a workflow that runs after R-CMD-check.yaml succeeds on main/master and force-pushes the checked commit to test. The sync is skipped when test holds commits that are not reachable from main, so unmerged work is never overwritten. Push experimental changes to test and each push to main resets it again.

use_workflow_test_branch(path = dir)
#> ✔ Created workflow: /tmp/RtmplqzxOK/.github/workflows/sync_test_branch.yml
#> → It runs after "R-CMD-check.yaml" succeeds for "main/master", then syncs the
#>   checked commit to "test".
#> → If "test" has unmerged work, the sync is skipped automatically.

Check system dependencies

Some packages need system development libraries (graphics and font libraries, for example) to compile. check_sysdeps() detects the package manager in use (dpkg, rpm, pacman, apk or brew), checks each dependency with it, and reports every hit and miss together with a ready-to-paste install command for the missing ones.

check_sysdeps()

With deps = NULL (the default), a built-in list of graphics and font libraries (freetype, libjpeg, libpng, libtiff, libwebp, harfbuzz, fribidi, fontconfig) is checked using the names that the detected package manager expects. Pass your own names in deps, and optionally set manager to check against a manager other than the detected one:

try(check_sysdeps(c("freetype-devel", "libwebp-devel"), manager = "rpm"))

The result is returned invisibly as a named logical vector, so it can be reused in scripts. Set verbose = FALSE to keep the run silent:

ok <- check_sysdeps(verbose = FALSE)
ok[!ok]

Detect the Positron version

get_positron_version() reports the version of the Positron IDE that hosts the current R session. It is useful for diagnostics, bug reports, or for enabling IDE-specific behaviour only on recent builds.

get_positron_version() # e.g. "2025.01.0"
get_positron_version(long = TRUE) # e.g. "2025.01.0-123"

The version is looked up in three steps, in this order:

  1. the POSITRON_VERSION environment variable set by Positron for its R sessions (POSITRON_LONG_VERSION, which also carries the build number, when long = TRUE);
  2. the .ps.positron_version() helper that the IDE injects into the session;
  3. the positron --version command-line tool.

If the session does not run inside Positron and no positron executable is on PATH, the function returns NA_character_ instead of throwing an error, so it is safe to call in any session, including CI.
